purpose: Re-audit the No.1/Ichigo-equivalent operation under current Branch B geography, aircrew regeneration, Pacific allocation, Burma no-U-Go, and Five-Go outcomes. Do not import historical Ichi-Go phase timing or older local-forward adjudications automatically.

historical_reference.historical_start: 1944-04-17/19 Honan opening; Hunan-Kwangsi phase late May
historical_core_objectives: capture/deny east and south China Allied airfields including Kweilin/Liuchow potential B-29 sites
reduce reliance on vulnerable sea transport by creating an overland corridor to Indochina
damage Nationalist field armies and political position

five_go_1943: Hanzhong captured 1943-07-21; Sichuan Phase III HOLD
branch_divergences.western_pressure: Hanzhong-Guangyuan remains an active front and air/recon pressure system; 36th/41st/17th divisions remain committed at 2.3-2.8 division-equivalents.
branch_divergences.chengdu_matterhorn: Japan can already impose recurring air-defense/logistics tax on Chengdu/Matterhorn from the Hanzhong system; ground conquest of Sichuan is not required to impose strategic pressure.
branch_divergences.burma: U-Go deep Imphal/Kohima offensive is NO-GO; this avoids a large IJA aircrew/airframe sink but does not make Burma divisions freely transferable to China.
branch_divergences.shipping: Branch sea transport is healthier than historical 1944; the continental Korea-to-Indochina corridor retains value as redundancy and occupation integration, but its emergency necessity is lower.
branch_divergences.nanjing: Expanded Nanjing/security apparatus releases about 3.0-3.8 Japanese division-equivalents of static workload theater-wide, enabling a concentrated Hunan field package without stripping every rear node.
branch_divergences.pacific_1944_04_30: Five-carrier Japanese system is nearing full combat integration; Central Pacific/Marianas remains the top marginal sink for premium aviation, engineers, communications and fuel. China receives its already prepared package but not unlimited top-grade additions.

northern_honan_phase.replacement: North China/12th Army conducts corridor security, local clearing, bridge/rail repair and anti-guerrilla operations as needed.
northern_honan_phase.caveat: Five-Go does not automatically prove the complete Peiping-Hankow through-line is repaired and secure; rail status remains a separate audit item.
northern_honan_phase.effect: No need to delay the Hunan main operation for a full historical Honan annihilation phase.

objectives: capture Changsha/Xiangtan transport and airfield nodes
force Fourteenth Air Force evacuation/demolition of nearby fields
phase_A.force: 10 divisions plus brigades; 60th Division held as theater reserve

conditions: limited continuous rail/bridge and Xiang River flow
650-850 t/day forward combat-supply flow for designated leading force
>=70% planned truck serviceability after Changsha phase
Fourteenth Air Force interdiction not causing multi-day transport collapse
phase_B.strategic_value: Hengyang remains a major rail/river/air junction and therefore a strong second objective.

phase_C.axis: Hengyang -> Lingling -> Kweilin/Guilin -> Liuchow/Liuzhou with possible Canton-side linkage
why_less_automatic_than_history: healthier branch sea transport reduces emergency need for a continental Southern Army corridor
Chengdu/Matterhorn already pays a standing air-defense tax from Hanzhong pressure
each southern advance lengthens a vulnerable inland logistics and occupation corridor
still_has_value: create strategic transport redundancy if achieved at acceptable cost

sichuan.reason: Five-Go Phase III remains HOLD; Hanzhong-Guangyuan pressure is more cost-effective than another deep mountain campaign.

air_reaudit.note: The Apr-25 Fifth Air Army gate predates the explicit branch aircrew-regeneration rule. Apply the regeneration effect to crewed/ready output, not raw aircraft production.
air_reaudit.interpretation: A 200+ Hunan ready concentration is plausible as a short surge, not a continuous theater assumption. Western Hanzhong/Sichuan pressure must remain credible.
air_reaudit.source_rule: JAPAN_AIRCREW_REGENERATION_SOFT_PROGRESS_1944-03-08_WORKING_v001: IJA land-based effective ready output 1.15-1.30 versus a static replacement model; this re-audit uses only a conservative portion because the prior China gate already contained some branch recovery.

timing_assessment.historical_comparison: The branch Hunan main attack begins about 2.5 weeks earlier than the historical late-May Hunan-Kwangsi phase, while the historical mid-April Honan phase is not replayed at full scale.
timing_assessment.do_not_accelerate_to_april: Air regeneration improves readiness, but final stocks, concealment, bridge/engineer positioning, truck serviceability and command synchronization remain the binding gates.

chinese_response_implications.western_tax: Chinese/Sichuan forces and air remain taxed by the Hanzhong-Guangyuan salient and Chengdu defense.
chinese_response_implications.hunan_ground: This may reduce freely transferable strategic reserve to Hunan, but Five-Go did not destroy the main Chinese field army and no automatic collapse is permitted.
chinese_response_implications.fourteenth_air_force: Fourteenth Air Force remains a major interdiction and airfield-denial opponent; stronger Japanese ready fractions improve the opening balance but do not remove the transport-interdiction gate.

legacy_forward_nodes.CHINA_ICHIGO_ANALOG_1944-05-27_08-06_FOR: REFERENCE_ONLY_DO_NOT_IMPORT; launch date/scale conflict with current gate and later branch audits
legacy_forward_nodes.rule: No future Changsha/Hengyang/Guilin/Liuzhou outcome is pre-awarded by this re-audit.

next_gate: At 1944-05-01 through D-day, adjudicate Chinese/Fourteenth Air Force detection, Japanese concealment, final air/engineer/fuel allocation and rail status in North China; then execute Phase A only.
